title: Choose Inspo's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Slide Library. Keep it, take a fused alternate, steer a re-roll, or play it straight.

options.label: The Slide Library
options.lineage: art-history slide libraries, 35mm lightboxes & carousel trays
options.body: Your saves become mounted 35mm slides glowing on a light table in a darkened room. The wall of everything IS the table: dense luminous frames on near-black, chrome receding to typed mount labels and grease-pencil marks. Design types are carousel trays; the filter row reads as tray dividers. Clicking a slide projects it — image large, beside the registrar's typed caption card carrying the style name, keywords, the hero-background prompt, and Copy Brief: the art-history lecture ritual ('this is Constructivism; note the diagonal axis') as product mechanism. Fire-and-forget saves land as still-developing frames that resolve into labeled slides when analysis completes. Honest risk: the luminous-slide treatment must be tuned so light screenshots don't blow out against the dark ground — mount and matting discipline has to be exact.

options.label: Fillmore Handbill
options.body: Fused: the gallery as a ballroom poster wall — hot orange on electric blue chrome, liquid hand-drawn lettering for tray names, the active filter vibrating at the ink boundary. Case: maximal anti-minimalism with deep designer resonance. Risk: vibrating complementary inks compete with the screenshots, which are the content.

options.label: Hand-Bent Neon
options.body: Fused: a dark studio where tray names run as hand-bent neon script and the active filter ignites cobalt; saves glow like sealed tubes. Case: real material glow, dark-room atmosphere, zero minimalism. Risk: signage is a one-word grammar — it decorates a wall of images rather than organizing one.
